classification.difficultyReason: Find a triangle angle before applying the converse co-interior angle theorem.

spec.description: Triangle AEB with C on AE, D on EB and internal segment CD. Embedded triangle CDE belongs to this same figure. No parallel marks or angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: Angle EAB = 45 degrees; angle AEB = 100 degrees; exterior angle CDB = 145 degrees. Drawn using base length 4.6 arbitrary units, apex at the intersection of rays at 45 and 145 degrees. CD endpoints share height; this placement does not add a printed parallel assertion.
spec.answerVisibility: All three givens retained; no derived angles or parallel markers.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABE&=180^\circ-45^\circ-100^\circ\\\angle ABE&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles in triangle $ABE$. Since $B,D,E$ are collinear, $\angle DBA=35^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CDB+\angle DBA&=145^\circ+35^\circ\\\angle CDB+\angle DBA&=180^\circ\end{align*}$$
Therefore $AB\parallel CD$ (converse of the co-interior angle theorem).
